page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg5.3xlarge is a high clock speed virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It is configured with an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6149 processor running at a base frequency of 3.1 GHz. The instance delivers 12 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 6 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. Memory capacity is 48.0 GB, resulting in a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware capabilities include AVX-512 instruction set support alongside standard integer manipulation and cryptographic extensions. There is no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistence, and baseline network throughput is rated at 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results reveal a divergence between single-threaded and multi-threaded processing. Single-core throughput is relatively restrained, with Geekbench single-core scoring 1100.0 and single-thread compression benchmarks placing in the lower quartile. In contrast, multi-threaded metrics remain within the mid-range distribution, achieving 10812.38 in stress-ng multi-core tests and a PassMark CPU score of 11929.55. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 56.31 GB/sec, while write operations achieve 39.44 GB/sec. Application testing displays moderate performance across operational tasks, recording 10.75 million Redis SET operations per second and 6.37 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance provides a predictable allocation of dedicated compute resources and 48.0 GB of memory without the added expense of integrated GPUs or local NVMe arrays. Tradeoffs include low single-threaded instruction speed, baseline networking capped at 2 Gbps, and reliance on remote block storage. Workload suitability centers on general multithreaded tasks, static web serving clusters, in-memory caching tiers, software compilation, and moderate database operations that do not require low-latency local drives.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg5.3xlarge is a dedicated virtual machine instance featuring 12 vCPUs and 48.0 GB of RAM powered by a 3.1 GHz Intel Xeon 6149 processor on the x86_64 architecture. Positioned within the high clock speed family, it features 6 physical cores with multithreading, a 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio, and support for AVX-512 instructions. The instance provides no integrated local disk storage and operates with a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate average multi-core processing performance, including a PassMark CPU score of 11929.55 and 10.75 million Redis SET operations per second, counterbalanced by lower-tier single-threaded output. It suits multi-threaded application servers, Redis caching, software compilation, and containerized web workloads.
